labelScope: run-34 script-audit directory (stable-staker-v2-cutover); labels are run-local and do not collide semantically with ledger labels of earlier runs

classifiedFindings.label: L-01
classifiedFindings.title: The Phase 6 per-user loss bound (ERC4626_MAX_LOSS_BPS = 2) sits inside autoDOLA's stepwise live spread, so :preview's go/no-go flips between blocks. The bound is enforced only in forge's local pass, so a regime step during the Ledger session lands a migration above 2 bps that only :verify's live-balance aggregate detects
classifiedFindings.faithfulnessNote: Deviates from story 082/083 per-user bound (<= 2 bps + 1000 wei) when it lands mid-session, and story 087 Concerns claim (verifier per-user check bounds total) is false. Mirror a pointer into spec-conformance.md; the primary entry stays L-01 in the QA report because the root cause is gate calibration/enforcement point, not a story mis-implementation.

classification.assetImpact: Staker principal in the DOLA (and in principle USDC) pool: an over-bound migration charges the live autopool round-trip spread to stakers. At current size ~2.09 bps of ~1,222.7 DOLA (~0.26 DOLA) total, of which the portion above the stated 2 bps spec is ~0.009 DOLA (<$1). The spread charge itself is socialized-by-design (F-02 wont-fix); only the over-spec residual and the lost gate guarantee are defects.
attackPath: 1. Operator runs :preview / forge local pass while autoDOLA is in a low-spread regime (<2 bps round trip) - all requires pass.
2. During the ~30-tx Ledger signing session, autoDOLA steps to its high-spread regime (observed 2.07-2.09 bps round trip, lasting ~22.5h).
3. Phase 6 transactions land on chain; the per-user require is not re-evaluated on chain, so the migration completes above 2 bps.
4. Resume/preview re-run and :verify per-user checks pass; only :verify's live per-pool aggregate reverts (short 0.008936 DOLA on fork), and it can be masked by ~0.009 DOLA of organic V2 stake.
classification.likelihood: low - requires an autopool regime step inside a single signing session; steps are discrete and observed hours-to-days apart
classification.assumptions: Cutover not yet broadcast; pool sizes as of block 25988932; autopool spread regimes as observed across 25981150-25988932
classification.externalRequirements: Tokemak autoDOLA/autoUSDC state-driven spread step between local pass and on-chain inclusion; operator broadcasting in that window
classification.availability: Go/no-go red for ~22.5h without code change. Fail-closed before any tx: V1 continues to operate, no funds locked, retry-able on regime change or after re-calibration. This is delay of a one-shot owner migration, not impairment of live protocol function. A stale progress file after a local-pass revert (by inspection, not executed) needs manual trimming - operational friction, not a brick.

classifiedFindings.justification: Medium requires either impaired protocol function/availability or a value leak with a stated attack path. Neither clears the bar: (a) the 22.5h red go/no-go blocks only an owner-initiated, not-yet-broadcast migration while the live V1 system keeps serving users, fails closed with zero transactions, and is retry-able - this is operational delay, not protocol availability loss; (b) the value path is dust (~0.009 DOLA over spec, ~0.26 DOLA total round-trip spread which is by-design socialized loss), needs an exogenous regime step inside a single signing session, and is still detected (not silently accepted) by :verify's aggregate. It is not downgraded to QA because it is fork-proven, the NatSpec rationale for the constant is empirically false, the only on-chain-landing detector is maskable, and a competent owner would be surprised that a green local pass bounds nothing about the landed Phase 6 txs (Law 3 footgun). Low.
classifiedFindings.borderlineNote: Two reviewer questions: (1) Medium-by-availability: rejected because the blocked function is a pre-broadcast owner migration, not a live user path; would reconsider if the cutover were time-critical (e.g. V1 deprecated/paused awaiting V2) or if the phantom progress-file state were proven to block resume non-trivially (currently by inspection only). (2) Magnitude scales with pool TVL: the over-spec leak is proportional (bps), so at materially larger pools (e.g. 100x) the same path could approach Medium value-leak; re-weigh if pool sizes grow before broadcast.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: 1) Re-derive ERC4626_MAX_LOSS_BPS in its own story from a multi-day sample of autoDOLA/autoUSDC previewRedeem/previewDeposit versus convertToAssets covering at least one up-step (observed max 2.07 bps round trip), e.g. 2x observed max (~5 bps); rewrite the L147-153 NatSpec to cite that sample. 2) In `_initiatePool`, for ERC4626 pools, pre-quote the round trip before `initiateMigration` (as already done for the market strategy): exit = previewRedeem(convertToShares(P)), re-deposit = convertToAssets(previewDeposit(credit)); log `LOSS_HEADROOM|token|bps` in preview and STOP AND REPORT when it exceeds the bound. 3) Runbook (//:broadcast): state that the Phase 6 bound depends on the autopool regime, that :preview must be re-run immediately before signing, that a :verify aggregate red right after a green local pass means the regime moved mid-session (resume will not detect it), and what to do with a progress file left by a local-pass revert (delete it when no transaction was sent). 4) Correct story 087's Concerns claim about the verifier's per-user check bounding the total, or add a per-user total (pre -> credited) check to the verifier, reconstructing pre-migration principal from the MigratedOut credit as credit*P/min(R,P).

classifiedFindings.label: Q-01
classifiedFindings.title: The cutover's //:broadcast key and Phase 7 NatSpec claim every Phase 7 halt point keeps the breaker live, but at halt 5 (after V2.unpause, before Pauser.register(V2)) a committed global Pauser.pause() does not reach StableStakerV2
classifiedFindings.faithfulnessNote: Documentation (//:broadcast key + Phase 7 NatSpec) overclaims breaker liveness at every Phase 7 halt; behaviour at halt 5 differs. Mirror a pointer into spec-conformance.md.

classification.assetImpact: None demonstrated: under a global pause at halt 5 all three Pauser-registered strategies pause, so V2 stake/withdraw/autoAnnihilate revert EnforcedPause and claim reverts 'claim disabled' (0 succeeding user entry points, fork-proven).
attackPath: 1. Phase 7 halts after V2.unpause() and before Pauser.register(V2) (halt 5).
2. An emergency coincides; operator calls Pauser.pause() relying on the documented guarantee.
3. V2.paused() stays false; the intuitive direct V2.pause() reverts onlyPauser; correct remedy is V2.setPauser(OWNER) then V2.pause().
classification.likelihood: very low - one-transaction window coinciding with an emergency
classification.externalRequirements: Halt at exactly step 5 plus a concurrent incident

classifiedFindings.justification: C4 'issues with comments' / doc-vs-behaviour with no reachable value path: strategy-level containment is fork-proven, the window is one tx and is the unavoidable trade-off of the L-05 fix, and a 2-tx remedy exists. Not Low because there is no state-handling defect and zero user exposure. Not Informational/dropped because the doc is operator-relied during an emergency and the obvious remedy reverts (non-obvious Law-3 consequence), so it must remain visible as an open tracked doc correction. QA.
classifiedFindings.borderlineNote: Would rise to Low if any V2 user entry point were reachable under a global pause at halt 5 (e.g. a strategy later unregistered, or a new V2 path not gated by strategy pause). Reviewer may argue Informational; recommend keeping QA for tracking since L-05 is proposed fixed and a note there would vanish.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Correct the //stable-staker-v2-cutover:broadcast doc key and the cutover NatSpec to name the halt-5 window: V2 is unpaused but not yet registered for one tx. Record its containment (all three strategies registered, so V2 value paths revert under a global pause) and the OWNER remedy (V2.setPauser(OWNER) then V2.pause(); a direct V2.pause() reverts). Optionally extend the Phase-8/preview GLOBAL_PAUSE probe to assert that V2 (and Antimatter) are actually paused after the simulated pause, not only that Pauser.pause() did not revert.
classifiedFindings.evidence: fork-logs/r34-gapfix-halt5.log: test_P7_halt5_globalPauseCannotReachV2 PASS. HALT5 registered=0; committed Pauser.pause() OK with V2.paused()=false; per-pool strategyRegistered=1 strategyPaused=1; stake/withdraw/autoAnnihilate REVERTS 0xd93c0665, claim REVERTS 'claim disabled'; 'user entry points that SUCCEED with V2 unreached=0'; remedies R1 direct pause REVERTS onlyPauser, R2 setPauser(OWNER)+pause WORKS, R3 register+second global pause REVERTS; resume converged, global pause reaches V2. Also in r34-gapfix-fullfile.log (19/19). Spot-reproduction.md item 3, Caveat 1: the audit's own test_P7_everyHaltPoint reports k=5 as LIVE because it checks only registered contracts, which is how this gap escaped the first pass.
